record.original_question: Prove that if Omega is a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain in C^n which is finite type in the sense of D’Angelo, then it is of finite type in the sense of Kohn (ideal type). Prize $50 -J. McNeal, mcneal@math.princeton.edu

evidence.quote: Prize Problem 2 Prove that if Ω is a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain in Cn which is finite type in the sense of D’Angelo, then it is of finite type in the sense of Kohn (ideal type). Prize $50 -J. McNeal, mcneal@math.princeton.edu

artifact.category_tag: finite type domains in several complex variables
artifact.status_search_result: For pseudoconvex domains with real-analytic boundary, the implication "D'Angelo finite type ⇒ Kohn finite (ideal) type" was established (Kohn 1979 via Diederich–Fornæss, with a direct proof by Brinzanescu–Nicoara). For general smooth pseudoconvex domains the implication does not appear to be settled in full generality; Siu's program on effective termination of the Kohn algorithm addresses related questions but the smooth case remains the focus of ongoing work.

status_evidence.title: Direct Proof of Termination of the Kohn Algorithm in the Real-Analytic Case
status_evidence.snippet: In 1979 J.J. Kohn gave an indirect argument via the Diederich-Fornaess Theorem showing that finite D'Angelo type implies termination of the Kohn algorithm for a pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary.
status_evidence.claim: The real-analytic case of the implication is known; a direct proof exists.

status_evidence.title: The Kohn Algorithm on Denjoy-Carleman Classes
status_evidence.snippet: The equivalence of the Kohn finite ideal type and the D'Angelo finite type ... has been extended to pseudoconvex domains in C^n whose defining function is in a Denjoy-Carleman quasianalytic class.
status_evidence.claim: Equivalence is known in quasianalytic classes, suggesting general smooth case remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain with smooth defining function $r$, so that $\Omega = \{r<0\}$ and $dr \neq 0$ on $\partial\Omega$. For a point $p \in \partial\Omega$, define:

(a) The D'Angelo type $\Delta_1(\partial\Omega, p)$ as the supremum, over all germs of nonconstant holomorphic curves $\varphi:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,p)$, of the ratio $v(\varphi^* r)/v(\varphi)$, where $v$ denotes the order of vanishing at $0$. The boundary point $p$ is of finite D'Angelo type if $\Delta_1(\partial\Omega, p)<\infty$.

(b) The Kohn ideal type (finite type in the sense of Kohn's subelliptic multiplier algorithm): starting with the multiplier ideal $I_0 = \sqrt{(r, \det(\partial\bar\partial r|_{T^{1,0}\partial\Omega}))}$ at $p$ (more precisely the ideal generated by $r$ together with the coefficient $\det$ of $\partial r \wedge (\partial\bar\partial r)^{n-1}$, taking real radicals at each step), and iterating Kohn's procedure of adjoining Jacobian determinants of generators and taking real radicals, $p$ is of finite Kohn type if this algorithm terminates with the unit ideal in finitely many steps.

Prove: if every boundary point $p\in\partial\Omega$ is of finite D'Angelo type, then every boundary point is of finite Kohn (ideal) type.
